recentReviews.title: SL Update Request
recentReviews.text:
Please make the SL update flow similar to Angel One.

Angel One provides a single input box, and the limit value is automatically updated based on the trigger value. In Zerodha, we currently have to update both the Limit Price and Trigger Price separately.

For quick intraday trades, this adds extra time and can cause missed entries. Please consider implementing the same single-input approach as Angel One, where the limit price is automatically adjusted when the trigger price is updated.

recentReviews.title: Serious order execution
recentReviews.text:
Extremely disappointing experience with this broker. I have lost thousands of rupees due to what appears to be an issue with order execution.
Orders are getting executed even though the price shown on the chart and the market depth does not appear to have reached my placed order price. This is extremely concerning, especially when trading involves real money and even a small difference in execution can result in significant losses.
I have personally suffered thousands of rupees in losses because of these executions. When the chart and market depth show that the specified price was not reached, an order should not be executed at that price without a clear and verifiable explanation.
A trading platform must provide accurate, transparent, and reliable order execution. Traders cannot be expected to trust a broker when their orders appear to be executed at prices that are not reflected in the displayed market data.
I strongly recommend that the broker investigate these executions, provide complete order/exchange execution details, and explain why the orders were triggered despite the displayed price not reaching the specified level.

 There have been instances where the buy average price shown on the platform appeared inconsistent with executed trades. If the displayed average price is incorrect and influences trading decisions, it raises questions about accuracy, transparency, and potential regulatory compliance.

recentReviews.title: Request to Add Trailing Stop Loss and Trailing Target in Kite App
recentReviews.text:
Hi Zerodha Team,

It would be extremely helpful if Kite could support trailing stop loss and trailing target functionality directly within regular order placement. Currently, users have to manually modify orders, which becomes difficult during fast market movements.

Suggested features:
- Trailing Stop Loss based on points or percentage  
- Trailing Target (profit lock-in as price moves favorably)  
- Ability to set both SL and Target together with trailing option  
- Applicable for intraday as well as delivery orders  
- Optional toggle inside bracket / GTT / regular orders  

This feature would significantly improve risk management and reduce the need for constant monitoring, especially for active traders.

Many modern trading platforms already provide trailing exits, and having this in Kite would make order execution much more efficient.

Please consider adding this in a future update.

recentReviews.text:
Zerodha trading app एक बेहतरीन और भरोसेमंद प्लेटफॉर्म है। इसका interface बहुत user-friendly है, जिससे नए और पुराने दोनों तरह के users आसानी से trading कर सकते हैं। App fast है, charts clear हैं और order place करना काफी simple है।

सबसे बड़ी खासियत इसकी कम brokerage है, जिससे trading cost काफी कम हो जाती है और profit पर ज्यादा असर नहीं पड़ता। Equity delivery पर zero brokerage और intraday में fixed charge होना इसे बाकी apps से अलग बनाता है।

इसके साथ ही Kite app की stability, real-time data और smooth performance trading experience को और बेहतर बनाती है। Overall, Zerodha एक safe, transparent और long-term trading ke liye best app है। ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

recentReviews.title: Missing Bracket Orders for Delivery Trades
recentReviews.text: The app is amazing. No doubt about it . But the only issue because of which me and my friends are going to move to another broker is the absence of Bracket Orders for delivery trades. Right now it is available only for intraday or else available to place every day which is not practical.  The need of the hour is to have a bracket order where we can specify entry, SL, Target and Qty in 1 single order valid for a year. The entry order gets triggered when the price reaches the specified price and only after the entry order is fulfilled, the SL/Trigger OCO order gets active. If other brokers can give it, why not the biggest broker in India???? Unless bracket order is implemented, we are moving to another broker. Will definitely return once this is made available.

recentReviews.title: 3rd CLASS TRADING APP
recentReviews.text:
Extremely disappointing trading experience. My order was clearly in profit, but when I tried to exit, the order failed or did not execute properly multiple times. I attempted to exit 2–3 times, but by the time the order finally went through, the position had moved into a loss.

This is a serious issue for a trading platform. In fast-moving markets, even a few seconds can make a huge difference. Traders should not have to repeatedly attempt an exit while their position is already in profit.

The overall experience was frustrating and unreliable. Groww seriously needs to improve order execution, stability, and reliability during market hours. I expected much better from a platform used for trading.

recentReviews.title: 3rd CLASS TRADING APP
recentReviews.text:
Extremely disappointing trading experience. My order was clearly in profit, but when I tried to exit, the order failed or did not execute properly multiple times. I attempted to exit 2–3 times, but by the time the order finally went through, the position had moved into a loss.

This is a serious issue for a trading platform. In fast-moving markets, even a few seconds can make a huge difference. Traders should not have to repeatedly attempt an exit while their position is already in profit.

The overall experience was frustrating and unreliable. Groww seriously needs to improve order execution, stability, and reliability during market hours. I expected much better from a platform used for trading.

recentReviews.title: Overcomplicated redesign is ruining a once-simple app
recentReviews.text:
As a long-time Upstox user, I am extremely disappointed with the direction this app is heading. I am not a daily day trader; I simply invest manage my portfolio, invest, and close the app until the next time. Upstox used to be great for this, but the recent design changes have turned a once-clean platform into a cluttered mess.
In the name of "upgrading," they have made basic navigation unnecessarily complicated. Finding standard services and essential portfolio details takes way too much effort now. The home page is crowded with irrelevant features that many of us never asked for:
 Unsolicited F&O & Strategy Tools: Pushing complex options trading strategies and trade ideas directly onto the homepage clutter is useless for long-term investors. Anyone who actively trades F&O already knows what tools they need; forcing it on everyone else just creates noise.
 Intrusive "Expert Advice" & Mutual Fund SIPs: Putting aggressive recommendations front and center makes the app feel cheap and chaotic. If someone wants to start a Mutual Fund SIP, they will intentionally navigate to the MF section—it doesn't need to take over the main screen.
Upstox needs to realize that adding more clutter isn't an upgrade—it's bad UX. Making the app hard to understand for simple, long-term investors will only drive customers away. If this bloated interface continues to prioritize pushed features over clean usability, I will consider closing my Demat account and shifting my portfolio to a simpler competitor.

recentReviews.title: Complaint Regarding Slow App Performance, Real-Time Data Delay and High Charges
recentReviews.text:
I am an active Upstox customer and would like to register a formal complaint regarding the poor performance of the Upstox trading platform.

The issues I am facing are:

1. The Upstox app loads very slowly, especially during market hours.
2. Real-time market data is not updating properly. Data freezes frequently and updates only after several seconds or sometimes minutes.
3. Charts and watchlists stop syncing regularly, making trading decisions difficult.
4. Order execution and price updates appear delayed compared to other broker platforms.
5. The platform performance becomes unreliable during volatile market conditions.
6. I also find the charges and fees comparatively high considering the quality of service being provided.

Due to these technical issues, I am unable to monitor the market accurately and there is a risk of financial loss. A trading platform must provide stable and real-time data without interruption.

recentReviews.title: From Upstox to Upstops
recentReviews.text:
I’ve been a user for the last 2 years, and the app has always been smooth and reliable. However, after the latest update, the overall experience has noticeably declined.

The new UI looks modern and clean, but performance has taken a hit. Navigation has become much slower than before, and portfolio values don’t refresh as quickly as they used to, which is frustrating during live market hours.

Opening charts now takes longer, affecting quick analysis and trading decisions. Another major issue is app continuity—when I minimize the app and reopen it, it rarely resumes where I left off. Instead, I often have to force close it from the background and launch it again, which becomes very inconvenient.

The redesign is visually appealing, but I hope the team prioritizes performance and stability in the next update. A fast and responsive experience is much more important for a trading app than cosmetic improvements.

recentReviews.title: Vegy good platform for traders
recentReviews.text:
I’ve been using Upstox for trading and overall it’s a decent platform with low brokerage and a clean interface. It’s beginner-friendly and charts are useful.

However, there are some serious issues during live trading. The app often lags or reconnects during high volatility, especially on expiry days. I also faced order execution problems where the wrong order type (GTT instead of intraday) got placed, causing losses.

If Upstox improves stability and execution speed, it can become one of the best apps. Right now, it’s good for learning but risky for fast intraday and options trading.

recentReviews.title: Overcomplicated redesign is ruining a once-simple app
recentReviews.text:
As a long-time Upstox user, I am extremely disappointed with the direction this app is heading. I am not a daily day trader; I simply invest manage my portfolio, invest, and close the app until the next time. Upstox used to be great for this, but the recent design changes have turned a once-clean platform into a cluttered mess.
In the name of "upgrading," they have made basic navigation unnecessarily complicated. Finding standard services and essential portfolio details takes way too much effort now. The home page is crowded with irrelevant features that many of us never asked for:
 Unsolicited F&O & Strategy Tools: Pushing complex options trading strategies and trade ideas directly onto the homepage clutter is useless for long-term investors. Anyone who actively trades F&O already knows what tools they need; forcing it on everyone else just creates noise.
 Intrusive "Expert Advice" & Mutual Fund SIPs: Putting aggressive recommendations front and center makes the app feel cheap and chaotic. If someone wants to start a Mutual Fund SIP, they will intentionally navigate to the MF section—it doesn't need to take over the main screen.
Upstox needs to realize that adding more clutter isn't an upgrade—it's bad UX. Making the app hard to understand for simple, long-term investors will only drive customers away. If this bloated interface continues to prioritize pushed features over clean usability, I will consider closing my Demat account and shifting my portfolio to a simpler competitor.

recentReviews.title: Critical Issues in Sell Order Functionality
recentReviews.text:
One of the most frustrating trading app experiences I’ve had.

When I click “Sell” from “Holdings,” the quantity should automatically be picked up from my actual holding quantity. Instead, it defaults to 1, forcing users to manually change it every time. This is a basic and potentially costly design flaw.

Also, by default, the order type is set to

“Market.” When I click on the “Market” input field, it should allow me to edit/select the order type and, if I choose “Limit,” immediately enable the Limit Price field for entering my desired price.

These are basic trading functionalities and common-sense UI requirements. Such a simple workflow should be seamless in any trading app.

If even these fundamental features are not designed properly, it seriously makes me question the quality and usability of the app. Please fix these basic issues instead of making users struggle with something that should be straightforward.

recentReviews.title: A REQUEST
recentReviews.text:
Dear Dhan Team,

I would like to appreciate the excellent work you’ve done with the Dhan DEX D3 platform. As an active F&O trader, I find it to be one of the best trading platforms available in India. The interface is clean, fast, and designed with traders in mind.

I have a few suggestions that I believe would make the platform even better.

1. Display P&L amount on Chart-based Target & Stop Loss

When placing a target and stop loss directly on the chart, the platform currently displays only the quantity. It would be extremely helpful if it also displayed the estimated profit or loss in monetary terms (₹), based on the target and stop-loss levels.

Seeing the actual amount at risk and the potential reward directly on the chart would improve decision-making and make trade management much more intuitive.

2. Reset Entry Price and P&L on Re-entry

This is the feature I would request the most.

Suppose I enter a contract at ₹200 and exit at ₹300. Later, I re-enter the same contract at ₹260. Instead of showing my fresh entry at ₹260, the chart continues to display an averaged or previous entry reference. This makes it difficult to judge the current trade accurately.

A bigger concern is the P&L display. For example, if I take a ₹10,000 loss on a contract, exit the position, and later find a fresh setup to re-enter the same contract, the platform still shows the previous ₹10,000 loss. Psychologically, this is distracting and can negatively influence trading decisions.

Every new position should be treated as a completely fresh trade. Once a position is closed, the next entry in the same contract should display:

* The new entry price only.
* Profit/Loss calculated only from the current open position.
* No carry-forward of the previous trade’s realized P&L on the active position display.

Traders can always view their overall realized P&L in the Positions, Orders, or Trade Book sections. However, the chart should reflect only the currently active trade, allowing traders to make unbiased decisions based on the present setup rather than previous outcomes.

I believe these enhancements would significantly improve the trading experience, especially for active intraday F&O traders.

Thank you for building such a powerful platform and for continuously improving it. I hope you will consider these suggestions in a future update.

Kind regards,

Areeb Khan

recentReviews.title: Regression, Not Progression – Bring Back Trailing Stop-Loss!
recentReviews.text:
I have been a loyal user of Dhan primarily for its superior execution features, but the latest update is a massive step backward for serious traders. The removal of the Trailing Stop-Loss (TSL) feature is unacceptable and significantly increases risk exposure for intraday players.

The latest update to the Dhan app is a massive regression in risk management and user experience. By removing the Trailing Stop-Loss (TSL) feature and restricting SL placement to only below the entry price, Dhan has stripped away the most vital tools for any disciplined trader.

Previously, one of the best things about Dhan was the "set and forget" convenience. I could take a trade, set my trailing SL, and go about my other work without being glued to the screen. Now, the app forces me into constant monitoring. Because I can no longer trail my SL into profit, I have to watch every tick. If I buy at 100 and the price reaches 145, I am forced to manually exit or risk a reversal hitting my original SL below 100. It has turned trading into a high-stress chore.

This update also ruins profit potential. To avoid a winning trade turning into a loss, I am now forced to set small targets of 10–20 points. If I aim for a 50-point target and the market hits 45 before reversing, I lose everything because I couldn't lock in gains at 30 or 40. Often, the trade hits my "forced" small target and then rallies to 50 anyway, meaning I’m missing out on significant moves just to play it safe.
Dhan collects its brokerage fees regardless of whether a trader wins or loses. However, by removing features that allow us to lock in profits, the platform is actively making it harder for users to survive. A trading app should empower its users with better technology, not take away essential safeguards. This update feels like a move to benefit the house rather than the trader.
I am extremely disappointed. This ignores the reality of market volatility and the basic principles of scaling out of positions. 

I strongly urge the Dhan team to restore the Trailing Stop-Loss and the ability to set SL above the buy price immediately. Until then, this is a 1-star experience for any serious trader.

I request the Dhan team to improve:

- Reduce lag during order execution and tracking

This improvement will greatly help traders like me who depend on quick and accurate data.

Looking forward to a faster and smoother experience in future updates.
